newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SEALS POLE AT NUERBURGRING.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SEALS POLE AT NUERBURGRING.

text.p: Australian Michael Doohan underlined his dominance of the 500cc class by sealing pole position for Sunday's German Grand Prix after Saturday's final qualifying session.

World champion Doohan, who has won seven of the eight races held so far this season, clocked a best time of one minute 38.425 seconds around the twisty, Nuerburgring circuit on a clear day with occasional sunshine.
The Honda rider, like most of his rivals, improved on the time he had set in gloomier weather conditions on Friday.
The second session was much tighter than the first one in which Doohan was well over a second faster than the rest of the field.
Spaniard Carlos Checa, on a Honda, was only 0.332 seconds slower than the runaway world championship leader with a second-best time of 1:38.757.
"I was surprised to be so much quicker than anyone else yesterday (Friday) because this is not a favourite place of mine," said Doohan, who has often been unlucky at Nuerburgring in the past.
"The bike seems to be working well and let's hope the weather will be all right for the race."
It was another impressive display of strength from Honda with Japanese Tadayuki Okada setting the third-fastest time of 1:39.069.
Last year's winner Luca Cadalora of Italy took the last place on the front row of the grid on his Yamaha.

Cadalora's fourth-best time of 1:39.187 in the last minute of the practice came as bad news to Frenchman Jean-Michel Bayle, who looked set to offer the new Modenas its first start among the front four.
His fifth-fastest time of 1:39.266 was nevertheless the best result obtained in qualifying by the futuristic looking, Kenny Roberts-built machine.
"It's a bit frustrating but it's not a bad result," Bayle said. "We've still got some work to do but everything is getting better."
In the 250cc category, local hero Ralf Waldmann, on a Honda, was deprived of pole position at the very last minute by Frenchman Olivier Jacque, also with Honda.

Qualifying specialist Jacque clocked a best time of 1:40.361 just as the chequered flag went down to signal the end of the session. Waldmann, who won here last year, had to be content with the second-fastest time in 1:40.785.
In the 125cc class, Italian teenager Valentino Rossi recovered from a disappointing first session to clock the best time in 1:47.160.
Aprilia rider Rossi, who admitted being too cautious after setting the fifth-fastest time in Friday's opening practice, has won six races already this season and will start hot favourite on Sunday.
